i-rename.prompt: Rename the function priceWithTax to grossPrice everywhere: where it is defined in src/billing/prices.ts, where it is re-exported in src/billing/index.ts, and every place that calls it.
i-rename.run: import * as b from './src/billing/index.ts'; import { dispatch } from './src/index.ts'; if (typeof b.grossPrice !== 'function' || 'priceWithTax' in b) throw new Error('billing exports: ' + Object.keys(b)); const r = dispatch({ method: 'POST', path: '/orders', body: { amount: 100 } }); if (r.status !== 201 || r.body.total !== 122) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r));

i-invoices.prompt: Add a POST /invoices endpoint. Create a new file src/handlers/invoices.ts with a createInvoice handler: it returns 400 with an error unless body.amount is a positive number (use isPositiveNumber from src/utils/validate.ts), otherwise 201 with body { amount, total } where total is priceWithTax(amount) from src/billing/index.ts. Register the route in src/routes.ts.
i-invoices.run: import { dispatch } from './src/index.ts'; const r = dispatch({ method: 'POST', path: '/invoices', body: { amount: 100 } }); if (r.status !== 201 || r.body.total !== 122) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r)); if (dispatch({ method: 'POST', path: '/invoices', body: { amount: -1 } }).status !== 400) throw new Error('no validation');

i-add-order-object.prompt: Change addOrder in src/db/orders.ts so it takes one object { net: number, total: number } instead of a number, and stores both fields on the order ({ id, net, total }). Update every place that calls addOrder.
i-add-order-object.run: import { dispatch } from './src/index.ts'; const r = dispatch({ method: 'POST', path: '/orders', body: { amount: 100 } }); if (r.status !== 201 || r.body.net !== 100 || r.body.total !== 122) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r));

i-refunds.prompt: Add a POST /refunds endpoint. Create a new file src/handlers/refunds.ts with a createRefund handler: it returns 400 with an error unless body.amount is a positive number (use isPositiveNumber from src/utils/validate.ts), otherwise it stores a refund with addOrder from src/db/orders.ts, whose total is minus the amount with tax (use the billing module's tax function), and returns 201 with the stored order. Register the route in src/routes.ts.
i-refunds.run: import { dispatch } from './src/index.ts'; const r = dispatch({ method: 'POST', path: '/refunds', body: { amount: 10 } }); if (r.status !== 201 || r.body.total !== -12.2) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r)); if (dispatch({ method: 'POST', path: '/refunds', body: { amount: 0 } }).status !== 400) throw new Error('no validation');

I2.description: Intent: as I1, but the caller starts first and the renamer 8 s later, Haiku
